questions.q: What are the four steps of the troubleshooting discipline taught throughout this path?
options: Guess, apologize, escalate, forget
Isolate, confirm, fix, document
Reboot, retry, report, close the ticket
Ignore, delay, reassign, archive
questions.explain: The discipline used across every troubleshooting lesson and the capstone's fixes is: isolate the specific cause, confirm it with evidence, fix it narrowly, and document it.

questions.q: A user reports a report 'just shows the wrong numbers.' What should you get before investigating further?
options: Nothing - start rebuilding the report immediately
The user's job title
The exact expected figure, the exact figure seen, and when each report ran
A signed change request form
questions.explain: Vague complaints need to become specific, provable problem statements first - the exact expected vs. actual figures and the timing of each report.

questions.q: When an FBDI load fails partway through, what should you check first?
options: Whether the internet connection was unstable during the entire load
The row-level and column-level error log the load process reports
Whether the file was saved in the wrong color scheme
Nothing - simply resubmit the exact same file immediately
questions.explain: Oracle's FBDI load process reports specific row- and column-level failures. Checking that error log first tells you exactly what needs fixing before reloading.

questions.q: A batch of subledger transactions shows accounting status Incomplete. Where should you look first?
options: The company's annual report
The user's email inbox
The general ledger's calendar setup
The Create Accounting error details for one specific transaction, which usually name a missing account rule mapping
questions.explain: Create Accounting's error detail for a specific transaction usually points directly at the missing piece, most often a missing account rule mapping.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should a consultant stop investigating and escalate instead?
options: Never - a consultant should always solve every issue alone
Immediately, before even isolating what the problem might be
Only if the client explicitly demands it in writing
When the problem is isolated to something outside Financials' own configuration, such as security, an interface, or infrastructure
questions.explain: Recognizing the boundary of what a functional consultant can fix - and looping in the right team once you've isolated an issue outside that boundary - is a sign of experience.
